query: Why are some incidents resolved inefficiently, and which underlying issues drive it?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents by domain gives a real grouping axis to compare resolution efficiency across issue types. Values align well with short_description (printer->printer_hardware, connectivity->network_connectivity).

per_column.name: issue_subtype
per_column.rationale: Finer-grained failure mode is useful for pinpointing drivers of inefficiency. Readings are sound ('not working'->device_not_responding, 'connectivity lost'->connectivity_failure), though 'device_not_responding' from vague 'not working properly' is a mild inference.

per_column.name: affected_asset_type
per_column.rationale: Asset type overlaps heavily with incident_category (printer/printer_hardware) but still adds some granularity (monitor vs keyboard_mouse). Mostly grounded, though 'network_device' for 'unable to connect to database' is a stretch since a DB issue may be software.

per_column.name: hardware_vs_software
per_column.rationale: A coarse hardware/software/network split is largely derivable from incident_category, so partly redundant, but a broad axis can still be useful for aggregate comparison. Values are reasonable readings.

per_column.name: reassignment_indicator
per_column.rationale: Reassignment is highly relevant to the inefficiency query. However the source text samples (short_description, timestamps) contain no reassignment evidence, and it contradicts resolver_workload_proxy (row 2: reassignment_indicator True but... consistent; row 3 False yet reassigned_resolver). The True/False values appear ungrounded in provided evidence and internally inconsistent with the workload proxy.

per_column.name: action_type
per_column.rationale: Action taken is a useful axis for efficiency analysis. But values like 'repair' for 'printer not working' are inferred defaults not stated in text; the text only reports symptoms, not remediation actions, so many values are confident specifics the source is silent on.

per_column.name: resolver_workload_proxy
per_column.rationale: Workload/reassignment is central to the query, but this contradicts reassignment_indicator on the same rows (row 3: reassignment False yet 'reassigned_resolver') and cannot be read from the sampled source text. Appears to derive from unseen columns at best; groundedness in shown evidence is weak and inconsistent.

per_column.name: urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Urgency framing is useful for prioritization analysis and is partly derivable ('connectivity lost on floor 3'->disruption_reported). 'standard' vs 'disruption' readings are mostly warranted, though somewhat subjective for terse descriptions.

judge.rationale: Most columns provide genuine grouping/comparison axes relevant to diagnosing inefficient resolution (category, subtype, urgency, workload), with some redundancy among incident_category, affected_asset_type, and hardware_vs_software. Groundedness is uneven: symptom-based categorizations are well supported by short_description, but action_type asserts remediation the text does not state, and reassignment_indicator vs resolver_workload_proxy are mutually inconsistent (row 3) and not supported by the sampled evidence, indicating hallucinated process signals.
